bib.title: Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Models

question: Do image diffusion models memorize and regenerate individual training images, and how do modeling and data choices affect this privacy leakage?
hypothesis: Diffusion models do not merely generate novel images: they memorize and emit training examples, and are less private than GANs.
contributions: Definitions of approximate image extraction (l,delta) and eidetic memorization (k,l,delta)
A generate-and-filter black-box extraction attack on Stable Diffusion and Imagen
Controlled study of hundreds of CIFAR-10 diffusion models: membership inference, inpainting, deduplication, DP-SGD, canaries
Comparison of diffusion models and GANs on membership inference and extraction

method.summary: Black-box generate-and-filter attack: pick near-duplicated training captions (CLIP embedding similarity), generate 500 images per prompt, flag cliques of >=10 near-identical generations (tile-wise l2) as memorized, then verify against training set. On CIFAR-10, train 16 diffusion models on random halves and run untargeted extraction, loss-threshold and LiRA membership inference, inpainting attacks, and compare to GANs.
method.task: training data extraction / membership inference against image generative models

datasets.name: LAION subset used by Stable Diffusion
datasets.preprocessing: near-duplicates found via 512-d CLIP embeddings and cosine similarity; captions of near-duplicated images used as prompts

datasets.name: Imagen training set (non-public)
datasets.split: top-1000 most duplicated prompts; 500 most outlier images
datasets.preprocessing: outlierness = mean CLIP distance to 1,000 nearest neighbours

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.split: each model trained on a random 50% partition
datasets.preprocessing: dedup experiment: imagededup similarity >0.85 removes 5,275 of 50,000

other.sampling: PLMS default, 512x512; timestep-resampled generation (~10x faster) for attack

models.name: CIFAR-10 diffusion models (16 shadow/target)
models.architecture: OpenAI Improved Diffusion or own re-implementation

other.count: 256 models per architecture, each on random 50% of CIFAR-10

models.name: Off-the-shelf GANs and DDPMs (WGAN-ALP, E2GAN, NDA, DiffBigGAN, StyleGAN-ADA, DDPM, OpenAI-DDPM)

training.objective: standard diffusion noise-prediction loss (Eq. 1) for CIFAR-10 models

other.GAN steps: BigGAN raised to 200,000 steps; StyleGAN and MHGAN StudioGAN defaults
other.DP-SGD: diverged on CIFAR-10 even at epsilon around 50
other.reference: OpenAI CIFAR-10 model: 500,000 steps at batch 128 = 64M examples (Appendix C.1)

inference.decoding: PLMS (Stable Diffusion); DDIM (CIFAR-10 per Table 3); inpainting per Lugmayr et al.
inference.samples: 500 images per prompt for 350,000 prompts (175 million) on SD; 500 per prompt for 1,000 prompts on Imagen; 2^16 images from each of 16 CIFAR-10 models (2^20 total); 2^20 per GAN; 5,000 inpaintings per target, top 10 scored kept, 100 images

parameters.strong LiRA: 20 Monte Carlo noise samples plus horizontal flip augmentation
parameters.inpainting: mask left half; 60% central pixels in Appendix D

metrics.name: extracted images
metrics.definition: generation with l2 <= delta to a training image (Definition 1); CIFAR uses adaptive per-image threshold

metrics.name: TPR at fixed FPR
metrics.definition: membership inference true positive rate at 1% or 0.1% FPR

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance of generated vs real

baselines: classifiers (<20% TPR at 1% FPR, from Carlini et al. 2022)
eval.protocol: Single run counts; manual visual inspection of top-1000 SD generations; no seeds or significance tests stated except a p<1e-261 overlap argument

availability.data: LAION and CIFAR-10 public; Imagen data non-public

limits: Extraction definition is deliberately narrow (l2-based); recognizable but non-identical generations (e.g. Obama) not counted
SD and Imagen results target heavily duplicated images and are an upper bound; no low-duplication extraction found on SD
Imagen training data non-public, so no visual examples
No hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, batch, hardware) given for CIFAR-10 models; no seeds or confidence intervals
Authors concede question of whether models copy vs generalize remains open

terms.definition: x is extractable if an efficient algorithm A not given x outputs x_hat = A(f) with l(x, x_hat) <= delta
x is extractable and at most k training examples are within delta of x
